cards.back: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss of electrons, Reduction Is Gain. Oxidation state rises on oxidation.
Oxidizing agent is itself REDUCED (gains electrons — MnO₄⁻, O₂, F₂). Reducing agent is itself OXIDIZED (loses electrons — metals, I⁻).
O = −2 (peroxides −1); H = +1 with non-metals; sum of states = overall charge; free elements = 0.
Oxidation at the anode (negative), reduction at the cathode (positive); electrons flow anode → cathode through the external wire.
External power supply forces non-spontaneous redox: anode POSITIVE, cathode NEGATIVE — reversed versus voltaic. Remember: AN OX / RED CAT, polarity differs by cell type.
A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal's ions from solution (Zn displaces Cu²⁺; Ag cannot).
Acid = proton donor; base = proton acceptor. Conjugate pairs differ by one H⁺ (HCl/Cl⁻, NH₄⁺/NH₃).
pH = −log[H₃O⁺]; pH + pOH = 14 at 298 K. [H₃O⁺] = 10⁻ᵖĥ when pH is a whole number.
Strong = fully ionized (HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄). Weak = partially ionized (CH₃COOH, H₂CO₃, HF) → higher pH, lower conductivity at equal concentration.
Acid − H⁺ = its conjugate base. Strong acids have extremely weak conjugate bases (Cl⁻ does nothing).
Can act as acid or base: H₂O, HCO₃⁻, HSO₄⁻. Water self-ionizes: 2H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + OH⁻ (Kw = 10⁻¹⁴ at 298 K).
Strong + strong: exactly 7. Weak acid + strong base: > 7. Strong acid + weak base: < 7. The flask contents at equivalence decide it.
Colour-change range must bracket the equivalence pH: phenolphthalein (8–10) for weak acid/strong base; methyl orange (3–4) for strong acid/weak base.

cards.front: Oxidation state of Mn in MnO₄⁻?
cards.back: +7: four oxygens at −2 give −8; total charge −1 → Mn = +7. Sum of states = charge.
Salt + water + CO₂. (Acid + reactive metal → H₂. Both are gas-releasing reactions worth memorizing.)

cards.front: Why is 0.1 M ethanoic acid a weaker conductor than 0.1 M HCl?
cards.back: Weak acid partially ionizes → fewer mobile ions → higher pH, lower conductivity. Same concentration, different ionization.
Strong acid + strong base salt → neutral (7). Weak acid + strong base → basic (CH₃COONa). Strong acid + weak base → acidic (NH₄Cl).
Give differences between two things point by point — e.g. competitive vs non-competitive, strong vs weak acids. Both sides required.
Reduction: electrons on the LEFT (Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al). Oxidation: electrons on the RIGHT. Balance O with H₂O, H with H⁺, charge with e⁻.
